# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

+# train is the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework — the
+# release-provenance job is the sole `--draft=false --latest` flip point),
+# but the per-creating-job guards (scripts/release_draft_guard.sh) cover
+# only their own job's failure. A train that dies UPSTREAM of the publish
+# point (core tests -> quality-gate red -> binaries skipped ->
+# release-provenance skipped) left the staged draft orphaned: the creating
+# run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never fire), the failed train is
+# superseded and never rerun, and verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST
+# tag only — so the draft rotted exactly 24h until the daily sweeper
+# deleted it and filed the recurring sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728).
+#
+# Called from the ci.yml `train-draft-guard` job, which needs
+# release-provenance and runs with `if: always()`: by the time this script
+# runs, the publish point has settled (success, failure, or skip) and every
+# in-train draft-creating job (binaries, web-spa, build-extension) has
+# settled with it.
+#
+# Deletes (by release id, the tag itself is never touched — drafts may
+# carry an empty tag_name, and the id-based API delete is what the sweeper
+# uses) only drafts for THIS train's tag whose well-formed
+# `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker names a COMPLETED run:
+# a superseded failed train will never publish them, and draft assets are
+# unpublished by definition (issue #282 E2 — published releases are the
+# artifact store). Fail-safe keeps — the sweeper remains the backstop:
+#   - a FAILED or CANCELLED publish point (rerunnable — the draft is the
+#     rerun --failed recovery vessel, gh-1899 convention);
+#   - drafts owned by a run that is still queued/in_progress (a concurrent
+#     creator leg, e.g. build-macos.yml from the daily cli leg, may be
+#     mid-upload — the train can fail faster than a sibling workflow
+#     finishes attaching);
+#   - unmarked drafts (no marker = no proof of pipeline ownership — E1,
+#     gh-2008; a human draft is never deleted here);
+#   - any owner-run status lookup failure (never delete blind).
+#
+# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY; needs `contents: write` (release delete) and
+# `actions: read` (owner-run status probe — same grant model as the
+# sweep-drafts job, review of #294).

+tag="${1:?usage: release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
+repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

+# needs.release-provenance.result). Deletion is only correct when the
+# publish point is UNREACHABLE: `skipped` means its needs (binaries) failed
+# or were skipped, and `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
+# jobs — nobody will ever publish this draft. A FAILED or CANCELLED
+# provenance IS rerunnable, and the staged draft is then the rerun

+# recovery vessel") — keep it; the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is
+# never recovered. Unset (wiring broken) keeps too: fail-safe, never

+# parsing: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching body yields an EMPTY
+# stream, so the array wrapper keeps exactly one (possibly empty) value
+# per draft row.
+rows=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --arg tag "$tag" '
+  [ .[] | select(.draft == true and (.tag_name // "") == $tag)
+    | { id: (.id | tostring),
+        run: ([ (.body // "")
+                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
+                | .run ]
+              | .[0] // "") } ]
+  | .[]
+  | [ .id, .run ] | @tsv')

+deleted=0
+kept=0
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r id marker_run; do
+  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
+  if [ -z "$marker_run" ]; then
+    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag carries no release-draft-owner marker — no proof of pipeline ownership (possibly a human draft, E1); leaving it to the 24h sweeper (issue #282)"
+    kept=$((kept + 1))
+    continue
+  fi
+  # Fail-safe lifecycle check: delete only when the owner run has
+  # COMPLETED. A non-completed status — or any lookup failure (403 without
+  # actions:read, API blip) — keeps the draft: never delete blind.
+  # Explicit jq pipe (not gh's --jq): mirrors sweep_stale_drafts.sh, where
+  # every JSON probe is filtered by a real jq stage.
+  status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
+    | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+  if [ "$status" != "completed" ]; then
+    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag is owned by run $marker_run (status: ${status:-<lookup failed>}) — the owner is not provably done; refusing to delete a possibly mid-upload draft. The 24h sweeper remains the backstop (issue #282)"
+    kept=$((kept + 1))
+    continue
+  fi
+  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id"
+  echo "::warning::train draft guard: deleted draft $id for $tag (owner run $marker_run completed; this failed train is superseded and will never publish it — a rerun cannot resurrect skipped jobs). Draft assets are unpublished by definition; the git tag is untouched (issue #282, gh-2230)"
+  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
+done <<< "$rows"
+
+echo "train draft guard: deleted=$deleted kept=$kept for $tag"

184 AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

content.text:
Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then

      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already

      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)

        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, OR the body carries a well-formed
#     `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   stale + pipeline (bot author or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { bucket: (
          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  case "$bucket" in
    fresh)
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      [ -n "$run_url" ] || run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \

find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing

    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \

      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee ai-teammate 2>/dev/null || true)

  fi
  rm -f "$body"

  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ sweep found nothing stale — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{

File('${bin.path}/gh').writeAsStringSync('''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "\$*" >> "\$GH_LOG_FILE"
cmd="\$1"

# Permission enforcement (review of #294): mirror the GITHUB_TOKEN scope
# each subcommand needs, so a workflow forgetting to grant one fails TESTS
# instead of dying silently in production (gh run list 403s without
# actions:read and the sweeper's || true hides the dead "creating run"
# feature). GH_STUB_PERMISSIONS is a space-separated granted-scope list;
# unset means full access.
granted="\${GH_STUB_PERMISSIONS:-*}"
need=""
case "\$cmd \$2" in
  "run list"|"run view"|"run watch"|"run rerun") need=actions ;;
  "issue "*|"label "*) need=issues ;;
  "release "*|"api"*) need=contents ;;
esac
if [ "\$granted" != "*" ] && [ -n "\$need" ] \\
   && ! printf '%s\\n' "\$granted" | grep -qw "\$need"; then
  echo "gh: HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration (stub: '\$cmd \$2' needs '\$need'; granted: '\$granted')" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "\$cmd" in
  api)
    case "\$2 \$3" in
      "-X DELETE"*) : ;;
      *) cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/releases.json" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  label)
    case "\$2" in
      # gh-1134: view succeeds only when the fixture label exists; create
      # self-heals it (unless label-create-fails is planted) — mirrors real
      # GitHub: create is idempotent-failure when the label already exists.
      view) [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-exists" ] && exit 0 || exit 1 ;;
      create)
        if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-create-fails" ]; then
          echo "gh: label create failed (stub)" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        touch "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-exists" ;;
      *) : ;;
    esac
    ;;
  pr)
    case "\$2" in
      list)
        if printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--state closed'; then echo 0
        elif printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q 'headRefName'; then echo 0
        else cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/open-pr.txt" 2>/dev/null || true; fi ;;
      *) : ;;
    esac
    ;;
  run)
    if [ "\$2" = "list" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--workflow'; then
      # gh-2105: the sweeper's tag-train lookup
      # (gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch <tag>) — served from
      # train-runs.json when planted, an empty array otherwise. The
      # plain --branch fallback below must keep hitting runs.tsv (the
      # existing creating-run fixtures).
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-runs.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-runs.json"
      else
        echo "[]"
      fi
    elif [ "\$2" = "view" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--json jobs'; then
      # gh-2105: the failed-train job names (gh run view <id> --json jobs).
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-jobs.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-jobs.json"
      else
        echo '{"jobs":[]}'
      fi
    elif [ "\$2" = "view" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--json status'; then
      # gh-2230: the train-level draft guard probes the draft-owner run's
      # lifecycle status; run-status.json when planted, completed otherwise.
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/run-status.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/run-status.json"
      else
        echo '{"status":"completed"}'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): the ci.yml tag
# train is the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework — the
# release-provenance job is the sole `--draft=false --latest` flip point),
# but the per-creating-job guards (scripts/release_draft_guard.sh) cover
# only their own job's failure. A train that dies UPSTREAM of the publish
# point (core tests -> quality-gate red -> binaries skipped ->
# release-provenance skipped) left the staged draft orphaned: the creating
# run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never fire), the failed train is
# superseded and never rerun, and verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST
# tag only — so the draft rotted exactly 24h until the daily sweeper
# deleted it and filed the recurring sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728).
#
# Called from the ci.yml `train-draft-guard` job, which needs
# release-provenance and runs with `if: always()`: by the time this script
# runs, the publish point has settled (success, failure, or skip) and every
# in-train draft-creating job (binaries, web-spa, build-extension) has
# settled with it.
#
# Deletes (by release id, the tag itself is never touched — drafts may
# carry an empty tag_name, and the id-based API delete is what the sweeper
# uses) only drafts for THIS train's tag whose well-formed
# `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker names a COMPLETED run:
# a superseded failed train will never publish them, and draft assets are
# unpublished by definition (issue #282 E2 — published releases are the
# artifact store). Fail-safe keeps — the sweeper remains the backstop:
#   - a FAILED or CANCELLED publish point (rerunnable — the draft is the
#     rerun --failed recovery vessel, gh-1899 convention);
#   - drafts owned by a run that is still queued/in_progress (a concurrent
#     creator leg, e.g. build-macos.yml from the daily cli leg, may be
#     mid-upload — the train can fail faster than a sibling workflow
#     finishes attaching);
#   - unmarked drafts (no marker = no proof of pipeline ownership — E1,
#     gh-2008; a human draft is never deleted here);
#   - any owner-run status lookup failure (never delete blind).
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY; needs `contents: write` (release delete) and
# `actions: read` (owner-run status probe — same grant model as the
# sweep-drafts job, review of #294).
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# The publish point's settled result (exported by the workflow from
# needs.release-provenance.result). Deletion is only correct when the
# publish point is UNREACHABLE: `skipped` means its needs (binaries) failed
# or were skipped, and `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
# jobs — nobody will ever publish this draft. A FAILED or CANCELLED
# provenance IS rerunnable, and the staged draft is then the rerun
# --failed recovery vessel (the gh-1899 convention in ci.yml's success-path
# dedupe step: "a red provenance keeps the draft as the rerun --failed
# recovery vessel") — keep it; the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is
# never recovered. Unset (wiring broken) keeps too: fail-safe, never
# delete blind — the sweeper backstops the kept drafts either way.
result="${PROVENANCE_RESULT:-}"
if [ "$result" != "skipped" ]; then
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: release-provenance ${result:-<result not exported>} — a rerunnable (non-skipped) publish failure keeps the staged draft as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention); the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is never recovered (issue #282)"
  exit 0
fi

# ── inventory: drafts for THIS train's tag ──────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them (same shape as sweep_stale_drafts.sh). Ownership-marker
# parsing: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching body yields an EMPTY
# stream, so the array wrapper keeps exactly one (possibly empty) value
# per draft row.
rows=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --arg tag "$tag" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true and (.tag_name // "") == $tag)
    | { id: (.id | tostring),
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | .[]
  | [ .id, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=0
kept=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id marker_run; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  if [ -z "$marker_run" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag carries no release-draft-owner marker — no proof of pipeline ownership (possibly a human draft, E1); leaving it to the 24h sweeper (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  # Fail-safe lifecycle check: delete only when the owner run has
  # COMPLETED. A non-completed status — or any lookup failure (403 without
  # actions:read, API blip) — keeps the draft: never delete blind.
  # Explicit jq pipe (not gh's --jq): mirrors sweep_stale_drafts.sh, where
  # every JSON probe is filtered by a real jq stage.
  status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$status" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag is owned by run $marker_run (status: ${status:-<lookup failed>}) — the owner is not provably done; refusing to delete a possibly mid-upload draft. The 24h sweeper remains the backstop (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id"
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: deleted draft $id for $tag (owner run $marker_run completed; this failed train is superseded and will never publish it — a rerun cannot resurrect skipped jobs). Draft assets are unpublished by definition; the git tag is untouched (issue #282, gh-2230)"
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
done <<< "$rows"

echo "train draft guard: deleted=$deleted kept=$kept for $tag"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  # gh-2042 (review): ONE call for the WHOLE list — the gate's contract is
  # per-call all-or-nothing ("refuse before any upload"), so per-asset
  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view
  # snapshot (N round-trips, a wider draft→published TOCTOU window, and a
  # partial mutation when an early benign asset uploads before a later
  # fa-* refusal).
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"

  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED

sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write

    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45

    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit

**Summary**: The train-level draft lifecycle guard correctly closes the gh-2230 orphaned-staged-draft class: deletion is gated on the publish point being provably unreachable (`PROVENANCE_RESULT == "skipped"`), scoped to the trained tag, marker-ownership-proven, and fail-safe on every unprovable case (in-flight owner run, unmarked/human draft, lookup failure, unexported result). **Key Issues** (ranked digest — non-blocking, no rework required):

1. `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh:92` — SUGGESTION: the lifecycle keep-check reads only the marker (creator) run; a sibling creator leg attaching to the same draft from a *different* run (e.g. the build-mobile.yml leg losing the E3 create race, per `release_attach_or_create.sh` docs) is not covered, although the ci.yml/docs rationale cites "a concurrent creator leg may be mid-upload" as a keep-reason (docs/ci.md:206). Deleting mid-attach 404s that leg's upload — the attach path has no recreate fallback — reddening an unrelated scheduled run once; the next leg recreates the draft and the 24h sweeper backstops. The pre-existing sweeper carries the same race, so this is residual-risk documentation more than a defect.
2. `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh:49` — NIT: "nobody will ever publish this draft" and "a rerun cannot resurrect skipped jobs" hold for `gh run rerun --failed`, but a full `gh run rerun` re-evaluates the whole graph — binaries/provenance re-run and attach-or-create mints a fresh draft that then publishes. The deletion stays safe (the draft object is gone; a rerun recreates it by design); soften the absolute wording in the script/ci.yml/CHANGELOG comments.

No `ci_failures.md` present; no previously-raised findings registry; first review round (no new hunks file).
